intro.title: Conditional Rendering with Ternary
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue component that displays a dynamic message based on a condition. You will learn how to use the ternary operator for conditional rendering directly in your template. The main technologies involved are Vue's template syntax and JavaScript's ternary operator. This approach allows you to show or hide content efficiently with a concise, inline expression. By the end, you'll be able to control UI elements based on state changes in a clean, readable way.
intro.usecase: Conditional rendering with ternary operators is essential for creating responsive interfaces that adapt to user context. In e-commerce sites, you'll see this pattern when showing 'Add to Cart' vs 'Out of Stock' buttons based on inventory status. Dashboard applications use it to toggle between 'Loading...' spinners and data visualizations when fetching completes. Form validations frequently employ ternary operators to display error messages only when input fails checks, keeping interfaces clean until needed.
